articles.title: A Split Decision: Supreme Court Shields Fed's Lisa Cook, But Hands Trump Broad Power Over Other Agencies
articles.summary: In a dramatic 5-4 ruling, the Supreme Court blocked President Trump's attempt to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook — the first Black woman on the board — while her case proceeds. But in a separate 6-3 decision, the Court gave Trump sweeping authority to fire leaders of other independent agencies, overturning a 91-year-old precedent.

articles.title: Supreme Court Overturns 91-Year Precedent, Grants Trump Sweeping Power to Fire Independent Agency Leaders
articles.summary: In a 6-3 ruling, the Supreme Court gave President Trump the power to fire Federal Trade Commission members at will, overturning the 1935 Humphrey's Executor precedent. The decision marks a major expansion of presidential control over agencies once designed to be independent, effectively ending bipartisan requirements at the FTC.

articles.title: Israeli Assault in Southern Syria Displaces Villagers; Turkey Condemns 'Flagrant Violation' of International Law
articles.summary: Israeli forces shelled the Syrian village of Abdin on Sunday night, forcing residents to flee. The attack is part of a surge in Israeli military operations in Deraa and Quneitra provinces, with nearly 300 incidents recorded in June. Turkey and Syria condemned the incursion as a violation of sovereignty.
